findings.reason: a worker performing the stated reproduction either records the wrong behaviour in the gate log or adds `--reason`/`--run` on its own initiative, so the section's reproduce-before-repair step does not exercise the path its own cases drive.
findings.text: the reproduce-first sentence seeds "a widen of a run in a temporary crew home whose worker record names a live stand-in process", but `widen_claim` refuses any non-self widen while `record_process_alive(pointer) is True` (`reckon/crew/claims.py:106`), so that arm returns the ClaimAmendmentRefusedError text ("its worker is still running; wait for that process to exit"), not the `ok` result with `write_paths` that nova-39 saw; the defect is only observable through a self-widen, which the first test case names and the reproduction does not

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `crew_widen` is at `reckon/crew_run_commands.py:1658`, `claims.widen_claim` at `reckon/crew/claims.py:64`, `record_process_alive` at `reckon/crew/process_liveness.py:300`; the new comment's evidence resolves (`attempt-1-worker.json` pid 183824 at 13:52:24Z, `attempt-2-worker.json` pid 195147 at 13:54:05Z, and `stream.jsonl` lines 3911/3961 carry the two EROFS records it describes).
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §8's reproduce-first step says "a widen of a run … whose worker record names a live stand-in process", but a plain widen in that state is refused, so the arm cannot observe the ok-result defect the section is about.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the reproduction output goes into the gate log and every log sits under the run directory, both durable; nothing in §8 is written to a session scratchpad or a node-local path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — `takes_effect` names the behaviour; §8 adds no plan label, ticket number or version tag, and its prose states the mechanism rather than any tracker reference.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — the stated cause holds: the widen's emitted result carries no timing word (`crew_widen` emits run_id/phase/node/session_id/added/write_paths/grants and nothing about mounts), and "a running worker's mounts are fixed when bwrap starts it" is confirmed by `attempt-1-worker.json`'s argv, which binds the worktree at launch; the section correctly scopes the replaced-tree cause out to §5 rather than blaming a widen.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §8 carries one deliverable (the widen result says when widened paths take effect); its three cases all serve it, and it is not merged with §5 even though both are about mounts.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §8 is declared `implementable` in `plan-section-declarations`, f-arolw-008 drives it with the matching `/reckon-build … §8` prompt, its `data-links=""` needs no section wait (it writes `crew_run_commands.py` and `claims.py`, which no other section writes), and the surviving s7→s6 wait still matches `plan-section-depends-on`.
